utility.notes: Menlo Park is a well-documented San Mateo County city, and San Mateo County is uniformly PG&E territory, consistent with PG&E service already established for other San Mateo County records this session.

value.name: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) - ECOplus (default)
value.notes: Confirmed directly via the City of Menlo Park's own page: 'WestLight Energy is the official electricity service provider for energy customers in San Mateo County.' The default product is ECOplus (50% renewable); ECO100 (100% renewable) is available as an opt-up tier; customers may also opt out entirely back to PG&E generation.

permit_authority.value: City of Menlo Park Community Development Department, Building Division

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other PG&E-territory records in this dataset.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes Menlo Park/San Mateo County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other PG&E-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.program_or_pathway: Photovoltaic Real Time (PRT) Permit (SB 379 automated real-time process)
other_conditions: Single-family residential, roof-mounted, new installations only (no upgrades or additions)
Electrical service must be 400A or less with no panel upgrades, and include a 225A disconnect switch and bus bars
Applicant must be a California-licensed contractor
Projects including battery storage or EV charger installations are currently ineligible for the automated real-time process
Menlo Park Fire Protection District approval is required before City permit issuance

permit_fees.notes: The page states processor (SolarApp+) fees apply but does not state the City's own permit fee amount.
